instantiated_cells.justification: The lobbyist definition turns on receiving "economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses" with no dollar floor, so any amount of compensation qualifies.

Wisconsin's lobbyist definition and licensing provisions contain no expenditure-based threshold for the lobbyist (the $500 trigger in §13.64 applies to the principal's registration, not the lobbyist's status).

The principal must itemize the lobbyist's name, address and total amount only "If the total amount of lobbying expenditures and obligations... made or incurred to any lobbyist for the principal exceeds $200 during the reporting period."

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is thereby exempted from licensing under §13.63, registration under §13.64, and the §13.68 reporting requirements (covering its lobbyist as well).

Wisconsin's exemptions and expense-statement provisions contain no percentage-of-compensated-time threshold exempting a lobbyist from filing disclosure; the only time-based gate is the 5-days-per-reporting-period definitional test in §13.62(11).

content.text:
I'll analyze each row carefully against the Wisconsin statute text.

**Analysis:**

1. **Lobbyist compensation threshold**: §13.62(11) defines "Lobbyist" as one who "is employed by a principal, or contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses, from a principal" — no dollar threshold for compensation.

2. **Lobbyist expenditure threshold (lobbyist-definition)**: The $500 in §13.64(1) is a PRINCIPAL registration trigger, not a lobbyist-definition expenditure trigger. WI has no lobbyist-side expenditure threshold for definition.

3. **Lobbyist time threshold**: §13.62(11) — "the individual is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period." Reporting period is 6 months per §13.62(12r).

4. **Itemization de minimis (per-lobbyist itemization on principal expense statement)**: §13.68(1)(a)6 — $200 threshold for itemizing payments to a lobbyist.

5. **Filing de minimis dollars**: §13.621(5) — $500 aggregate verified statement exemption.

6. **Filing de minimis time percent**: No percentage-of-compensated-time threshold for lobbyist filing exemption exists in the statute.

input.justification: The lobbyist definition turns on receiving "economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses" with no dollar floor, so any amount of compensation qualifies.

Wisconsin's lobbyist definition and licensing provisions contain no expenditure-based threshold for the lobbyist (the $500 trigger in §13.64 applies to the principal's registration, not the lobbyist's status).

Section 13.62(11) provides that where duties are not exclusively lobbying, an individual is a lobbyist only if they make lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period, which §13.62(12r) defines as a 6-month period.

The principal must itemize the lobbyist's name, address and total amount only "If the total amount of lobbying expenditures and obligations... made or incurred to any lobbyist for the principal exceeds $200 during the reporting period."

A principal anticipating aggregate lobbying expenditures/obligations not exceeding $500 in a calendar year may file a verified statement and is thereby exempted from licensing under §13.63, registration under §13.64, and the §13.68 reporting requirements (covering its lobbyist as well).

Wisconsin's exemptions and expense-statement provisions contain no percentage-of-compensated-time threshold exempting a lobbyist from filing disclosure; the only time-based gate is the 5-days-per-reporting-period definitional test in §13.62(11).
